review.meaning: customer-name overlays, customer number, boarder names and weekly-only amounts confirmed; the property address source is a material business decision.
openQuestions: RSFA-DECISION-1: which address is the 'property' on boarder declarations: legacy = 'Applicant 1 Physical Address' (free text) + 'Applicant 1 Residential City/Town' + 'Applicant 1 Residential Postcode/Zip' (two different sources on one address); proposal ANZ-ADDR-1..3 = 1st Property Address + its City + Postcode (preview PDF provided).

UNRESOLVED (bank template defect): 'Is this amount inclusive of food and/or bills (utilities)' Yes/No. Monday has dedicated status columns (color_mm3d16dh, color_mm3dm95k, Yes/No), but in ANZ's PDF both widgets of 'B1 Inclusive' and 'B2 Inclusive' export the value 'No' (/Opt ['No','No']); ticking Yes would still record 'No' in the form data. Left blank for the customer, as in the legacy configuration. Needs ANZ's corrected form or RSFA's decision to accept a visual-only tick.
'Customer number(s)' takes the single column 'ANZ Customer Number (if known)'; a second customer's number cannot be printed.
Customer name(s) are legacy overlays (rect / 1.2, inferred; docs/03); visually aligned on the dotted line.

corrections.decisionRef: RSFA-DECISION-1: which address is the 'property' on boarder declarations
corrections.reason: Proposed: print the security/purchase property (as BNZ Boarder). The legacy lines also mix two different Monday sources: the free-text physical address and the structured residential City/Town and Postcode columns.
corrections.evidence: The declaration describes the property where the boarders live (ASB: 'your main owner-occupied residence'). The legacy rule uses the applicant's physical address (OpenAI-split parts of text_mkzvrrfx); BNZ Boarder (tested, deployed) uses 1st Property Address (text_mkzvqaw7, split into Street/Suburb/City/Postcode by Make module 26). Both are in the Make contract. Which one is right depends on the deal (purchase vs refinance).
